specGaps: PRIORITY vs CONTIGUITY precedence (APPROVED as drafted): the 11.5 bullet wants same-group requests to dequeue contiguously, while 11.4 pins strict priority interactive<review<batch with FIFO within class. RESOLUTION: strict priority remains the OUTER order — 11.4's tested invariant is untouched — and contiguity applies only WITHIN a priority class; a higher-class arrival wins the next dequeue even if it breaks a group's run. Raised at the Phase 11 gate.

FAIRNESS MECHANISM (APPROVED as drafted): §2.2's affinity block is {header, contiguousDequeue} with additionalProperties:false, so the mechanism must need NO new config key. RESOLUTION: a selected group's contiguous burst covers only the members queued AT SELECTION TIME (members arriving mid-drain wait for the group's next turn); the next group is chosen by oldest-waiting head. Cross-class starvation stays governed by 11.4's strict priority + queueTimeoutMs, which is the pinned reading of 'a low-priority group still drains'.
contiguousDequeue:false (APPROVED as drafted): RESOLUTION — false makes affinity fully INERT; for any arrival sequence the observed order is identical to plain 11.4 priority+FIFO.

THE SEAM (RESOLVED against committed code): affinity exposes a PURE policy in conductor::router — given the queued entries' {priorityValue, optional groupId, arrivalOrdinal} plus the parsed Affinity config, choose the next entry (or produce a total order) — called by AdmissionController::grantNext under the mutex it ALREADY holds. Purity is what makes six of the seven rows deterministic doctests with no threads, no sleeps and no fake clock, matching 11.3/11.4's no-sleeps posture. Only the end-to-end row needs the live harness.

assertions.text: among QUEUED requests (a backlog formed behind the admission cap), requests sharing one group value dequeue CONTIGUOUSLY: once the policy selects a group, every same-group member queued at selection time and in the same priority class dequeues before any other-group or untagged request of that class — asserted on the OBSERVED dequeue order, never on internal queue state

groups interleave fairly rather than starving: with two same-class groups where group A keeps receiving NEW members while its burst drains, group B still fully drains within a bounded number of dequeues (the burst covers only members queued at selection time; the next group is the oldest-waiting head), and a batch-class group still drains once higher-class pressure clears — affinity introduces NO starvation beyond 11.4's strict-priority semantics

ordering is stable under arrival jitter: the dequeue order is a deterministic function of (priority value, group id, arrival ordinal) — replaying the SAME logical arrival sequence with different interleavings yields the IDENTICAL order every run; ties break on the arrival ordinal assigned under the queue lock, never on wall-clock time, and the test controls sequencing without sleeps

an untagged request NEVER jumps the queue: it never dequeues earlier than the position plain 11.4 order (priority class, then FIFO) gives it, and untagged requests keep FIFO order among themselves — grouped peers may be pulled FORWARD past it, but affinity never ADVANCES an untagged request

affinity reorders only WITHIN a priority class: a queued same-group member in a lower class never rides its group's contiguous drain ahead of ANY queued higher-class request, and a higher-class arrival mid-drain wins the next dequeue — 11.4's strict interactive<review<batch invariant survives affinity verbatim, asserted against the SAME committed AdmissionController the 11.4 rows pin

the group id comes from config.affinity.header via 11.3's ALREADY-PARSED RequestTags.group: a config naming a DIFFERENT header string groups by THAT header, and a request tagged only with the old name counts as untagged. The shipped "X-Conductor-Group" is config data, not a hardcoded constant — and 11.5 must not re-read the header itself, so this row is asserted end-to-end through the real Router

affinity.contiguousDequeue:false disables the reordering ENTIRELY: for the same arrival sequence the observed dequeue order is exactly plain 11.4 priority+FIFO, grouped and untagged alike (11.2 already pins parsing and the default true; this row pins the FALSE behaviour)
